title: Three Seasons and One Short Net
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：river　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 river 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the fisherman ① crossed the river that no boatman in the harbour would have measured, and he said the crossing was the whole of the season. The ② river, meaning the stream itself and not the net, ran three seasons and stayed unmeasured in the book; a river, he said, is the only thing in a harbour that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ river in that harbour had the same short net beside it, and the ④ river at the far pier, meaning the catch they kept for the children to land and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A river, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the fisherman said the measuring is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the river was the whole of the matter, meaning the course and not the stream. The ⑥ river, meaning the course and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; river, he said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both a stream and a course. He said the course is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ river had become a line in a logbook, and the logbook had become an argument about the short net. The ⑧ river of the whole thing, the fisherman wrote in July, was one harbour and three seasons of measuring; river, he said, is either the catch at the far pier or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ river I remember is the stream measured in the logbook, which closed in 1963 and is still measured as the quietest in the harbour. A ⑩ river, my mother said in 1965, is the only stream that improves by being measured; every river, she said, is a course that has agreed to look like a stream. She said the course was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 河流（指渔港里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 河流（指那条河流本身，与小小的渔网相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross the river 渡这一条河流
D. n. 河流（指留给孩子们起的那一网）
E. n. 河流之事（抽象总称，指一处渔港的河流之事）
F. n. 河流（指航海日志里写到、被测量的那一条）
G. n. 河流、流向（指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 流向（抽象总称，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: crossed the river that no boatman in the harbour would have measured
The river, meaning the stream itself and not the net
the river at the far pier
the river was the whole of the matter
the river had become a line in a logbook
The river of the whole thing
A river, my mother said in 1965

answers.why: cross the river 意为“渡这一条河流”，1956 年那位渔人把渔港里没有一位船工肯测量的一条河流做了一遍。
river 意为“河流”，指那条河流本身而不是小小的渔网，它经过了三个汛期而在簿子上没有被测量。
river 意为“河流”，指渔港里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一张小小的渔网。
river 意为“河流”，指最远那座码头的留给孩子们起的那一网，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
river 意为“河流、流向”，指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条流向就是那件事的全部。
river 意为“流向”，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条河流，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
river 意为“河流”，指航海日志里写到、被测量的那一条，到 1961 年这一条成了航海日志里的一行。
river 意为“河流之事”，渔人七月写道，整件事的河流之事是一处渔港和三个汛期的测量。
river 意为“河流”，我记得的是航海日志里测量过的那一条，1963 年归港了，至今仍被说成渔港里最安静的一条。
river 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，河流是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的河流。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1956 年那位渔人渡了渔港里没有一位船工肯测量的一条河流，他说这一遍才是那个汛期的全部。（cross the river）
那条河流，指的是那条河流本身而不是小小的渔网，经过了三个汛期而在簿子上没有被测量。（river）
那处渔港里每一条河流旁边都有同一张小小的渔网。（river）
最远那座码头那条河流，指的是他们留给孩子们起的那一网，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（river）
叔叔说这条流向就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那条河流。（river）
1965 年母亲说，河流是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的河流。（river）
answers: In 1956 the fisherman crossed the river that no boatman in the harbour would have measured, and he said the crossing was the whole of the season.
The river, meaning the stream itself and not the net, ran three seasons and stayed unmeasured in the book.
Every river in that harbour had the same short net beside it.
The river at the far pier, meaning the catch they kept for the children to land and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the river was the whole of the matter, meaning the course and not the stream.
A river, my mother said in 1965, is the only stream that improves by being measured.
